# `silk/git/local`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read the references of a local Git repository from its `.git` directory: `HEAD`, the loose
references under `refs/`, and `packed-refs`.

## When to use
Call [`LocalRefs.read`](#LocalRefs.impl.read) with the Git directory to get a `RefList` from `silk.git.refs`, then
look up the current branch with `RefList.head` or a name with `RefList.resolve`. Use
[`LocalRefs.gitDirectory`](#LocalRefs.impl.gitDirectory) to find the Git directory of a working tree, which is `.git` or the
directory that a `.git` file names. It reads files through the `FileSystem` service of
`silk.system.filesystem`, so tests can give files in memory.

## Details
A loose reference file holds an object id, or `ref: ` and the name of another reference. A loose
reference replaces a packed one of the same name. Symbolic references, such as `HEAD` on a
branch, have the name as their target and the id that the chain of names ends at. The result
has `HEAD` first, then the other references sorted by name, as `git show-ref` lists them. For a
linked worktree, `HEAD` comes from its own Git directory and the other references from the
common directory that its `commondir` file names.

## Errors
- `GitRefError` from `silk.git.refs` if `packed-refs` or `HEAD` is malformed, a chain of
  symbolic references loops, or the repository uses the `reftable` format.
- `FileError` if a file or directory cannot be read.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

## Gotchas
Loose reference files that cannot be read as an id or a `ref: ` line are skipped, as Git skips
them, and so are `.lock` files. Only references are read: this does not read objects, so a tag is
peeled only when `packed-refs` records it.

Import as `LocalRefs` with `import silk.git.local { LocalRefs }`.

<a id="LocalRefs.impl.gitDirectory"></a>

### Associated function `gitDirectory`

```silk
pub effect fn gitDirectory(worktree: &Path) -> Path
    ! GitRefError | FileError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut FileSystem | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the Git directory of the working tree at `worktree`.

#### Details

When `worktree/.git` is a directory, that is the Git directory. When it is a file, as in a
linked worktree or a submodule, the file holds `gitdir: ` and a path, absolute or relative to
`worktree`, and that path is the Git directory.

#### Errors

- `FileError` with reason `NotFound` if `worktree/.git` does not exist, or another reason if it
  cannot be read.
- `GitRefError.Malformed` if the `.git` file does not start with `gitdir: `.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the path.

<a id="LocalRefs.impl.read"></a>

### Associated function `read`

```silk
pub effect fn read(gitDir: &Path) -> RefList
    ! GitRefError | FileError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut FileSystem | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the references of the repository whose Git directory is `gitDir`: `HEAD` first, then
the loose and packed references sorted by name.

#### Details

A loose reference under `refs/` replaces a packed reference of the same name. A symbolic
reference, such as `HEAD` when a branch is checked out, has the name it points at as its
`target` and the id that the chain ends at. Its `id` is `None` when the chain ends at a
reference that does not exist, such as the branch of a new repository. A detached `HEAD` has
an id and no target. A tag has a `peeled` id when `packed-refs` records it.

For a linked worktree, whose Git directory has a `commondir` file, `HEAD` is read from `gitDir`
and the other references from the common directory.

#### Errors

- `GitRefError.Malformed` if `HEAD` or `packed-refs` is broken.
- `GitRefError.SymbolicLoop` if a chain of symbolic references is longer than five.
- `GitRefError.Unsupported` if the repository uses the `reftable` format.
- `FileError` if `HEAD` or a directory under `refs/` cannot be read.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

#### Gotchas

Loose reference files that hold neither an id nor a `ref: ` line are skipped, and so are
`.lock` files, as Git does. Per-worktree references other than `HEAD`, such as
`refs/bisect/`, are not read.

<a id="LocalRefs.impl.parsePackedRefs"></a>

### Associated function `parsePackedRefs`

```silk
pub effect fn parsePackedRefs(contents: &[u8]) -> RefList
    ! GitRefError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the references of the `packed-refs` file `contents`, sorted by name.

#### Details

The file has an optional `# pack-refs with:` line, then one `<id> <name>` line for each
reference. A line `^<id>` sets the peeled id of the reference before it.

#### Errors

- `GitRefError.Malformed` with the offset of the first broken line.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.
